subject: chemistry
title: The Gases We Breathe
welcome_lead: Take a deep breath: a mix of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases fills your lungs.
meta_desc: Discover the composition of the atmosphere in this KS3 chemistry adventure on air.
final_note: You now know exactly what's in the air around you.

concepts.def: About 78% of the atmosphere; mostly unreactive.
About 21% of the atmosphere; needed for breathing and burning.
Around 0.9% of air; a noble gas.
About 0.04% of air but increasing slowly.
The mixture of gases held to Earth by gravity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Air is a mixture of gases. About 78% is nitrogen and 21% is oxygen. The remaining 1% is mostly argon, with traces of carbon dioxide, water vapour and other gases.

78% N₂, 21% O₂, 1% other.
You breathe in oxygen and breathe out more carbon dioxide. Fires need oxygen too — without it, a candle in a sealed jar quickly goes out.

Oxygen test: a glowing splint relights.
CO₂ test: turns limewater milky/cloudy.
Hydrogen test: a lit splint gives a squeaky pop.
